entities.summary: Known as the "Birthplace of Portugal" or "The Cradle City", Guimarães played a crucial role in the foundation of the oldest nation state in the world, serving as its first capital and the site of the Battle of São Mamede in 1128, where Portugal secured its independence from the Kingdom of Galicia. It received its Foral around 1096, the first one ever, by Count Henry, father of the first king Portugal, Afonso Henriques, who's said to have been born in Guimarães. This historical significance has contributed to its architectural heritage, spanning from the pre-medieval period to contemporary times.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Guimarães played a pivotal role in Portugal's independence from Galicia with the Battle of São Mamede in 1128, securing its status as the oldest nation state. Its Foral around 1096 marked the first of its kind, solidifying its importance.
